clue.text: Sex, humour, drama, story, stars these ultimately make pictures

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the five listed words, the things 'these' refers to

explanation.surface: A list of the ingredients of a racy film or novel, which together make a hit picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes the last letters of Sex, humour, drama, story and stars. 'Pictures' sounds like films, but here it means medical images.
explanation.definitionFit: Radiographs taken in a hospital are photographic images, hence pictures.

clue.text: It can be played without holding playschool up

indicators.note: up, in a down entry, means the whole construction is read from bottom to top
holding means the outer word for without wraps around the play and the school

parts.note: ex means without, as in ex dividend
split as play school: Noh is a Japanese play form, and poly is short for polytechnic, a school

explanation.surface: Something you can play without having to keep hold of the nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'playschool' has to be split into play and school. 'without holding' puts the play and school inside the word for without, and 'up' then turns the whole thing to read bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A percussion instrument of wooden bars struck with mallets is something played.

clue.text: Caustic initially, after King Charles I died

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of the word after

parts.note: CR stands for Carolus Rex, Latin for King Charles
d is the abbreviation for died in genealogies

explanation.surface: A biting remark about the death of Charles I.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' looks as if it attaches to Caustic, but it picks the A of 'after'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitter and sharp, as in a cutting remark, is a synonym.

clue.text: Characterised by caution, they last out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of they last are put out of order

explanation.surface: Careful people outlast others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges THEY LAST. 'last out' reads as endure.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving furtively and quietly so as not to be noticed shows caution.

clue.text: Professional backing of number is forecast

parts.note: pro is short for professional

indicators.note: backing means the word for number is turned round, read from back to front

parts.note: a number is a song, as in a musical number

explanation.surface: A professional reversing a number is predicting something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing of' reverses the song word. 'number' reads as a figure, but here it is a musical piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's or expert's prediction of how things will turn out is a forecast.

clue.text: I entered the expected score for match

indicators.note: entered means the letter I goes inside the golfing term

parts.note: in golf, par is the expected score for a hole

explanation.surface: Someone claims they reached the anticipated tally in a game.
explanation.walkthrough: PAR is golf's standard score; I goes inside it. 'match' looks like a game, but it means a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that go together form a matching couple.

clue.text: Stranded and broke

explanation.surface: Shipwrecked and penniless.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship run aground on a reef is stranded, and a person or marriage in this state is ruined or penniless.

clue.text: Things look different when it's dark

indicators.note: look different signals that the letters of things are arranged differently

explanation.surface: The everyday observation that the world seems changed at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look different' rearranges THINGS. The definition is a phrase meaning 'after dark', in the plural sense of evenings.
explanation.definitionFit: Hours after sunset are dark, so the plural noun means evenings.

clue.text: It's right to feature directors

parts.note: to star is to feature, as an actor in a film
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Approval of putting company executives in the limelight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' looks like correct, but it means the right-hand side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship, the right-hand side when facing forward has its own nautical term.

clue.text: Sometimes we deport an alien

annotationWithheld.why: Clue 'Sometimes we deport an alien (5)': SWEDE is hidden in 'someS WE DEport', but the only word that could signal the hidden run is 'Sometimes', which also supplies the S, so one word does two jobs

clue.text: Clarinets taken wrongfully by a thief

indicators.note: wrongfully suggests the letters of the instrument word are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Musical instruments stolen by a burglar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken wrongfully' rearranges CLARINETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Larceny is theft, so one who commits it is a stealer.

clue.text: Prayer for mercy

explanation.surface: A plea to heaven for clemency.
explanation.definitionFit: A short blessing said before a meal is a prayer, and the word also means clemency or favour shown to the undeserving.

clue.text: Load cargo back into river boat

indicators.note: into means the turned-round loading word goes inside the river's name

parts.note: the Po is the great river of northern Italy

indicators.note: back means the word for loading cargo is read in reverse

parts.note: to lade is to load cargo onto a ship

explanation.surface: Instructions to put freight back on a river vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LADE into EDAL, which goes 'into' PO. 'river boat' looks like one phrase, but 'river' is wordplay and 'boat' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pedal-powered pleasure craft is a kind of boat.

clue.text: Bill, embraced by Miss immune to Cupid's darts, is not invincible

indicators.note: embraced by means the word for bill is held inside the schoolmistress's name

parts.note: from the rhyme 'Miss Buss and Miss Beale, Cupid's darts do not feel', about two Victorian headmistresses
a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab

explanation.surface: A bill hugged by a woman unmoved by love shows she can be beaten.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorothea Beale was a famous Victorian headmistress; a British schoolyard rhyme says she and Miss Buss felt no Cupid's darts. The definition 'is not invincible' stands in for 'is able to be defeated'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that can be defeated is the opposite of unconquerable.

clue.text: There's a 'war brewing up for maritime flier

indicators.note: brewing up suggests the letters are stirred into a new mixture

explanation.surface: A conflict is looming for a seabird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewing up' rearranges THERE'S A WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-winged seabird that skims the waves is an ocean flier.

clue.text: No longer in trouble out to sea from Dutch port

parts.note: a ship lying off the coast is out to sea
the Hook of Holland is a Dutch ferry port

explanation.surface: A sailor relieved to be safely at sea having left a Dutch harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone let off a charge or obligation has escaped difficulty.

clue.text: Neglected, because of the energy required, to clear up

parts.note: for can mean because of, as in jumped for joy
go means energy or vigour

indicators.note: up, in a down entry, means the word for clear is read upwards

parts.note: nett means clear, as in clear profit

explanation.surface: Something left undone because no one had the energy to tidy it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns NETT into TTEN. 'clear up' reads as tidy, but 'clear' is NETT and 'up' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Something left out of mind and overlooked has been neglected.

clue.text: In talks, wrapped up the agreement

indicators.note: in talks means we hear the word as spoken, not as written

parts.note: wrapped up means packed

explanation.surface: During negotiations, a deal was concluded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In talks' signals a sound-alike: PACKED, meaning wrapped up, sounds like the answer. The surface use of 'wrapped up' means finished, but in the wordplay it means parcelled.
explanation.definitionFit: A treaty or formal understanding between parties is an agreement.

clue.text: It's worth changing a method, that's casual

indicators.note: changing means the letters of worth are altered in order

parts.note: a way is a method of doing something

explanation.surface: Altering a technique is worthwhile, as long as it is relaxed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges WORTH; then A and WAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A remark made offhand and without care is casual.

clue.text: Drinks heavily in clubs and stirs .

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
to arouse someone is to stir them

explanation.surface: A clubber who drinks a lot and causes a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' reads as nightclubs, but it is the card suit, C.
explanation.definitionFit: To revel noisily with plenty of drink is to drink heavily.

clue.text: The colour of English vineyard

parts.note: a cru is a vineyard or its wine, as in grand cru

explanation.surface: Asking what shade an English vineyard is.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale unbleached fawn shade is a colour, often used of fabric.

clue.text: Angel about to deliver a bribe

indicators.note: about means the backer word goes around the word for deliver

parts.note: an angel is a financial backer of a show
to hand something over is to deliver it

explanation.surface: A heavenly messenger about to bring a corrupt payment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angel' reads as a celestial being, but in theatre it is an investor, a BACKER, which goes 'about' HAND. 'about to' looks like 'going to'.
explanation.definitionFit: An illicit payment slipped to someone under the table is a bribe.

clue.text: Rum issue is likely to be successful

parts.note: rum means strange or odd
issue means offspring, so a son

explanation.surface: A strange outcome is probably a winner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like the drink, but it is the British adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse priced below even money in betting is expected to win.

clue.text: Bridge players interrupted by greeting and confrontation

indicators.note: interrupted by means the greeting breaks into the run of players' letters

parts.note: in bridge the four players are North, South, East and West; here S, W and N
how do is a casual greeting, short for how do you do

explanation.surface: A card game disrupted by someone saying hello, which turns into a row.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interrupted by' puts the greeting between the first and second of the three players' letters. The four bridge seats are named by compass points.
explanation.definitionFit: A decisive final clash between rivals is a confrontation; in cards it is also the moment hands are revealed.

clue.text: Shrub French writer raised

indicators.note: raised, in a down entry, means the writer's name is read upwards

parts.note: Albert Camus was a French writer

explanation.surface: A French author grew a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns CAMUS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A bush or small tree whose leaves and berries are used as a spice is a shrub.

clue.text: . Derive from another writer

explanation.surface: Taking material from a different author.
explanation.definitionFit: To take something from someone else is to derive it from another; George Borrow was a nineteenth-century English travel writer.

clue.text: Robots a learner found in the country

parts.note: R.U.R., Rossum's Universal Robots, is Karel Capek's play that gave us the word robot
L is for learner, from L-plates on British learner drivers' cars

explanation.surface: Robots and a trainee discovered out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: R.U.R. is the 1920 Czech play that introduced robots. The adjective fits 'in the country', away from towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to farmland and villages rather than towns is the sense of this adjective.

clue.text: Established a company

explanation.surface: Founding a business.
explanation.definitionFit: Firmly set up and secure means established, and a business partnership or concern is a company.

clue.text: Scholar. — one failing in this subject at school

parts.note: an MA, a Master of Arts, is a scholar

indicators.note: failing means the letter for one goes missing from the following word

parts.note: one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A learned person admits that someone is flunking this school subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one failing in this' removes I from THIS, leaving THS.
explanation.definitionFit: Arithmetic and algebra are taught as a core school subject under this short name.

clue.text: Kind of ship that at first gains favour with sailors

indicators.note: at first takes only the opening letter of the word that

parts.note: to win favour is to gain it
the crew are a ship's sailors

explanation.surface: A vessel that quickly becomes popular with seamen.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel driven by two propellers is a type of ship.

clue.text: It's a problem, taking care of sister at a party

parts.note: c/o, written CO, is the abbreviation for care of on letters
a nun is a religious sister
a drum was an old word for a large evening party

explanation.surface: A dilemma about looking after one's sister at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: DRUM for an eighteenth-century social gathering is an old sense crosswords still use.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzling question or riddle is a problem.

clue.text: Girl making witty remark

explanation.surface: A girl who comes out with a clever quip.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a female first name, and a quick sharp retort is also called by this word.
